answer: Because the orchard index resolves every citation against the hollow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the velvet audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 174 aliases hence burns the authoring cost 174 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 21 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
